items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1972-05-27
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] Well, Uncle, your Uncle Natty. [INTERVIEWEE] Uncle Natty in Chicago?

ctx.x: Yeah, he said it was Italian.

items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1969-12-30
items.q: Uncle Natty and I were, he was one of my favorite uncles... I visited him quite a number of times.

ctx.x: What about Natty? Did you know Natty Dominique when he was down here?

Oh, sure. Uncle Natty and I were, he was one of my favorite uncles. He was the younger one. Uncle Natty. And Uncle Natty went to war. And he was a mutilary in the war. And I remember the first time he came back. And he came to the estate up there on Grey Court Street. He didn't stay too long. And he left in Chicago. And I visited him quite a number of times. After I got my band. And I'd go and play up in the eastern part of the states. And Uncle Natty would be one of the first ones that I would go to see him.…
Did you, in playing, back in the chorus band, in playing stock arrangements and everything, did they change them around much? Not very much. You wouldn't put your own?

items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1961-05-11
items.q: Manuel lived right opposite Uncle Natty's house on Erdworth Street. And I used to watch Manuel when he'd come in from work and when he'd leave.

ctx.x: Natty had to do that with Manuel Perez.

That's right. A long time. A lot of the old time teachers were that way. Well, Manuel lived right opposite Uncle Natty's house on Erdworth Street. And I used to watch Manuel when he'd come in from work and when he'd leave. In the evenings, I used to follow the parades. I used to follow the bands. That's the one that Louie came out of. I used to love to hear those kids play those horns. I'd follow them for blocks.
That's a tuxedo or the honours band.
